source_evidence.quote: After adjustment for confounders, including diet, HRs per 1-SD were 1.06 (95% CI 0.91-1.22) for total dairy, 1.02 (0.88-1.18) for milk and 1.04 (0.90-1.20) for yogurt.
Our findings suggest no major role for dairy consumption in T2D prevention after MI.
Total dairy was inversely associated with T2D risk (RR: 0.97 per 200-g/d increment; 95% CI: 0.95, 1.00;P= 0.04;I(2)= 66%)
Included were prospective cohort studies that examined the association between dairy and incident T2D in healthy adults.

A text-supported contextual difference is that A studied drug-treated post-MI patients aged 60-80 y, whereas B pooled prospective cohorts of healthy adults (A sentence 3-4; B sentence 5), a population difference that A itself frames as the open question ('Whether dairy affects T2D risk after myocardial infarction (MI) is unknown', sentence 2).
